item: CapitalEnvelope grants are signed with symmetric HMAC-SHA-256: any cell that can verify a grant can also mint one
why: EnvelopeIssuer signs with qip_core::hmac_sha256, a symmetric primitive: the same key verifies and mints, so a compromised or malicious cell that can check a grant can also forge one. The module's own doc comment names the missing production requirements verbatim (asymmetric signatures, an HSM/key store, key rotation, per-envelope revocation, replay scoping) and calls the current scheme 'adequate for a single-operator deployment and for tests, and not adequate for production.' This is exactly one of the three in-tree-crypto gaps `.claude/rules/architecture/00-boundaries.md` names as still open ('asymmetric signing, a CSPRNG, and anchoring the event-log chain are three gaps no in-tree code may close — see ADR 0043 (proposed)'), and is independently confirmed in `docs/blueprint/assessment/GOV.json` (GOV-012), `SEC-b1.json` (SEC-001) and `CONTRACT-b1.json` (CONTRACT-004), all tagged against the same gap. Cannot be closed in-tree under ADR 0002/0009 (two dependencies only); it needs a dependency-class ADR for an asymmetric primitive before code changes, which is what ADR 0043 (proposed) is for.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §13 (Capital Brain & Capital Bank — 'autonomous treasury transfer inside signed corridors and hard caps')
GCP v2.1 §15 (Security and Trust Architecture)

item: Evidence-weighted capacity-aware capital sizing is fully implemented but never populated in production: CentralPlane.proposals is always empty, so CapitalAllocator::allocate runs on zero strategies every cycle
why: StrategyProposal (which carries the CapacityModel every capital-sizing decision is supposed to respect) has exactly one insertion path into CentralPlane's `proposals: BTreeMap<StrategyId, StrategyProposal>` — `set_proposal`, called only from `central/learning.rs`'s private `resize()`. `resize()` itself only mutates a proposal that must already exist (`self.proposal(strategy)?`), so nothing in non-test code ever performs the original insert; `grep -rn 'StrategyProposal {' backend/crates/runtime backend/crates/apps` outside tests returns nothing, and `grep -rn 'CapacityModel::new\|CapacityModel {'` over the same scope returns nothing. `CapitalAllocator::allocate(&proposals, ...)` (plane.rs:1576,1709, reached every DECIDE cycle from platform.rs:7214) therefore always allocates against an empty proposal list in production today. The machinery reads as a working, evidence-driven, capacity-bounded allocator — API surface, 127 crate tests, a public setter and getter — while being structurally inert, which is the same shape `.claude/rules/domains/risk-and-execution.md` names as the thing not to add ('a control that cannot fire reads as protection and is not'). This is a sizing feature, not a live-capital path, so it is not blocked by ADR 0099's conflict register; wiring a real proposal source in is ordinary in-tree work.
blueprint_refs: v11.6 §13 (capital grants to strategies/regions with expiry, capacity and drawdown limits)

item: The seven-veto TransferGate (CorridorAuthority/Caps/MinimumInterval/StatedPurpose/SourceBalance/VelocityAndAnomaly/KillSwitch) is fully implemented and hardened but has no production emitter — deliberately, and documented as such
why: `grep -rn "GateCommand {" backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime` outside tests returns nothing — confirmed independently. But `pre_positioning.rs:22-31` states the reason in the kernel's own module doc: a `GateCommand` carries the three enforcement-point attestations of custody class, corridor signature and destination allowlist, and those 'are facts a human establishes out of band... A machine that manufactured them from its own plan would be attesting to itself, which is the control measuring itself.' Building an automatic emitter would be the defect, not the fix. `platform.rs:7583` shows the kernel already validates a Gate command's funding field when one arrives, so the seam is wired correctly and simply unused — matching ADR 0021's paper boundary and the blueprint's own 'begin shadow-only' directive (v11.6 §30, Phase 10) for anything requiring an external, human-attested act. Independently corroborated by `docs/blueprint/assessment/RISK.json` (RISK-001). Retained as-is; do not build an emitter without an owner decision that resolves ADR 0099's conflict C1 (autonomous treasury transfer is LIVE_CAPITAL/EXTERNAL_ACTION and structurally blocked).

item: The crate name 'qip-capital-fabric' and its FabricJournal/FabricCommand/FabricState types collide in name with the blueprint's platform-wide native Rust Event & Control Fabric (fabricd, fabric-schema, fabric-mirror, ...), which is a distinct, not-yet-built subsystem

No code defect exists today (the two never share a wire format because the real Fabric does not exist yet), but the name collision is a documentation/clarity hazard for whoever builds C2's Fabric next to a crate already called 'capital-fabric' with its own FabricCommand/FabricJournal/FabricState vocabulary. item: qip-edge-node (the only binary that constructs qip-brokers' venue adapters, and the intended host for qip-execution-engine's OMS at the edge) is deployed to no environment — execution_nodes = {} everywhere
why: 89 tests in qip-brokers, 105 in qip-execution-engine, all structurally paper-only, and none of it runs anywhere: `execution_nodes = {}` in every tfvars, confirmed directly. This is not neglect — dev's tfvars header explains precisely what blocks it: ADR 0035 authorises exactly one node (newyork-1, shadow mode, dev only) but no boot image has ever been baked (the bake workflow exists and has never been dispatched), and ADR 0045 proposes a capital allocation figure without setting one ('a number a person chooses and no workflow may pick'). ADR 0099's conflict C8 separately notes billing is disabled on the dev project today, so `deploy.yml` cannot even push an image. Needs: an owner to (1) dispatch the image bake per `docs/operations/deploying-an-edge-cell.md`'s documented sequence, (2) set the capital allocation ADR 0045 proposes, (3) resolve the billing block named in C8 — none of which an agent may do unilaterally.

item: Two independently-defined margin models exist with no shared type and no reconciliation: qip-brokers::ledger::MarginPolicy (per-venue account, Reg-T defaults) and qip-capital::margin::MarginModel (central-plane portfolio margin with a concentration add-on)
why: MarginPolicy models what a simulated venue would require of one account (initial/maintenance fractions for long and short, defaulting to Regulation T); MarginModel models the central plane's own portfolio-wide margin (initial/maintenance rate plus a concentration add-on above a threshold). They may be legitimately different concerns — venue-quoted margin vs. platform risk margin — rather than true duplication, but nothing in either crate states that relationship, no shared trait or conversion exists between them, and their defaults (Reg-T vs. an arbitrary concentration threshold) could silently diverge from what the other believes is true collateral. Needs evidence: a product decision on whether AccountLedger's venue-reported margin should feed or be reconciled against qip-capital's MarginModel (per v11.6 §14's 'Counterparty/Venue' and 'Capital' risk domains, which name exactly this reconciliation), or whether the two are deliberately independent and should say so in their module docs.

item: OriginationMandate::admit (the five-gate market-creation approval, hard-capped at $250M) is fully implemented and tested but called from no composition root

item: qip-lifecycle's corridor::emit (the function that actually derives a CorridorPolicy/CorridorRuling from strategy standings) has zero production callers; only the plain data record CorridorSubject is referenced from the kernel

item: qip-mesh's six data-mesh ports (Lakehouse/Analytical/HotSeries/MasterData/Graph/Evidence) are implemented, tested and never constructed by any composition root; every managed-GCP MeshProvider target unconditionally returns Error::Unavailable
why: Confirmed independently: none of MeshLakehouse/MeshAnalytics/MeshHotSeries/MeshMasterData/MeshGraph/MeshEvidence, nor the six port traits, appear in kernel or app non-test source. This is a designed-ahead-of-the-store-decision port abstraction (the provider explicitly refuses to silently fall back to a local store when configured for a managed target, which is the right failure mode), and it is exactly ADR 0099's conflict C4: BigLake/BigQuery/Bigtable/Spanner/Spanner Graph/GCS-WORM are the blueprint's named backing services, and ADR 0002/0009 permit only serde+serde_json today. FileBacking (the one working implementation) is real file I/O — read_to_string/create_dir_all/write-then-rename — suitable for dev/single-node only, not the multi-region target. Needs an owner storage-record ADR per store, which ADR 0099 says the ledger should get first.

item: qip-mesh::spine implements only centre-to-cell hub-and-spoke dispatch (CapitalDispatcher down, CellDeltaReceiver up); no peer-to-peer inter-cell Reflex Mesh exists, though v11.6 §17 requires cells to exchange compressed opportunity/edge state directly with peers for cross-region 2-20-leg arbitrage — an architecture conflict with standing ADR 0008 ('Cells decide alone') that is not yet in ADR 0099's conflict register
why: spine.rs's own module doc states the topology directly: 'the wire between the nine regional cells and the central plane' — every CapitalDispatcher's 'peer' (spine.rs:275,308,323) is, from the centre's perspective, one cell, not another cell. v11.6 §17 requires a materially different shape for arbitrage coordination: 'Reflex nodes publish compressed executable edge states... to peers or regional coordinators' over a mesh that is explicitly 'deliberately separate' from the durable Fabric this crate's sibling channel resembles, and §30's Build Order names 'Multi-Region Reflex Mesh... peer mesh, opportunity tokens, distributed reservations, 2-5 leg cycles' as Phase 4's exit capability, growing to 3-20 legs in Phase 5. Today's centre-only fan-out cannot carry that traffic without going through the centre on every hop, which the blueprint explicitly rules out for latency-sensitive coordination. This is independently corroborated by `docs/blueprint/assessment/MESH-b1.json` (MESH-003: 'no peer channel exists'). ADR 0008 ('Cells decide alone... regional low-latency execution is separate from centralised training and portfolio intelligence, and the split is load-bearing') is a standing decision under `.claude/rules/10-product-direction.md`; per that rule, no code change may reopen it — this needs its own conflict-register entry and an owner ADR, the same way ADR 0099 treats C3/C7/C8, before any peer-mesh code is written.
